This is a beta of Nebula v2, which runs Super Mario Galaxy as native code built from SMGCommunity's Petari decompilation, on Windows, Linux, macOS and Android. You need your own copy of the game. A beta is for trying the game and telling us what breaks: expect faults, and keep a copy of your saves.

## Downloads

| System | Download |
|---|---|
| Windows 10 or 11 (x64) | [Nebula-Beta-Setup.exe](https://github.com/keepvaibin/nebula/releases/download/v2.0.0-beta.1/Nebula-Beta-Setup.exe) |
| Linux (x86-64) | [Nebula-Beta-Linux-x64.tar.gz](https://github.com/keepvaibin/nebula/releases/download/v2.0.0-beta.1/Nebula-Beta-Linux-x64.tar.gz) |
| macOS 12 or later (Intel and Apple silicon) | [Nebula-Beta-macOS.zip](https://github.com/keepvaibin/nebula/releases/download/v2.0.0-beta.1/Nebula-Beta-macOS.zip) |
| Android 12 or later (64-bit ARM) | [Nebula-Beta-Android.apk](https://github.com/keepvaibin/nebula/releases/download/v2.0.0-beta.1/Nebula-Beta-Android.apk) |

`SHA256SUMS` lists the SHA-256 of each download. The `.sig` and `.manifest` files are what Nebula's updates check before they install a new version. A beta is offered the next beta and the final 2.0.0; Nebula 1.0.2 is not offered the beta.

## Install

**Windows:** run `Nebula-Beta-Setup.exe`. Setup asks for your disc image and installs Nebula for your account.

**Linux:** unpack the archive, then run `./install.sh` in its folder. It asks for your disc image, then whether to install for your account or as a portable folder.

**macOS:** unzip the download and move `Nebula.app` to Applications. It runs on Intel Macs and on Apple silicon. Nebula is not signed by Apple: the first time, open it from **System Settings > Privacy & Security > Open Anyway**. On macOS 14 or earlier you can instead Control-click the app and choose Open. The included `How to open Nebula.txt` has the steps.

**Android:** install `Nebula-Beta-Android.apk`, open it, and choose your disc image.

Nebula reads Super Mario Galaxy for Wii from North America (RMGE01), Europe (RMGP01) or Japan (RMGJ01), as an ISO, RVZ or extracted folder.

## What is in

- Native code on Windows (Direct3D 12, Direct3D 11 or Vulkan), Linux and Android (Vulkan), and macOS (Metal).
- A home screen with Play, Settings, Benchmark and Quit, and updates from within the game.
- Upscaling, anti-aliasing, ambient occlusion, enhanced lighting and HDR options.
- Frame interpolation above 60 Hz.
- PlayStation, Steam, Steam Deck and other controllers, with gyro pointing on controllers that have motion sensors. Co-Star mode with a second controller.
- Cutscene skip with a confirmation, and dialogue speed up to Instant.
- Save import and export in the game, from a Wii, Dolphin or the Switch release, and Mii import.
- 34 achievements and play statistics.
- Menus in all 14 of the game's languages, and error codes with a saved report.

## What is not in

- Mods. This beta has no mod support: no Mods page, no `.luma` files, no LumaKit.
- The rework of the game's code that is still to come. This beta is the game as it stands, and the final 2.0.0 comes after that work.

## Speed

We make no promise about speed, stutters or smoothness in this beta. On a phone or tablet that runs at 120 Hz, the in-between pictures are uneven today.

## What we have not played ourselves

We test on one Windows computer and one Android tablet. The Linux package and the Mac app (Intel and Apple silicon) were built and started on GitHub's machines, and nobody has played them through yet. Everything else is untried: other graphics cards, other Android devices, other controllers.

## Report a fault

Report problems on the [issue tracker](https://github.com/keepvaibin/nebula/issues). Say which system and which graphics card or device you have, and what you were doing.

When Nebula stops, it shows an error code and saves a report in the `crashes` folder of its data folder: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Nebula\crashes` on Windows, `~/.local/share/Nebula/crashes` on Linux, `~/Library/Application Support/Nebula/crashes` on a Mac. Attach both files of the report (the `.txt` and the `.dmp`). On Android, choose **Share the game's log** in the settings and attach it.

If the game is slow, run the benchmark in **Settings** > **System** > **Benchmark** and choose **Send to developer** on its result, when the game offers it. The result has your graphics card and the frame times, and it tells us where to look.

## Requirements

- **Windows:** Windows 10 (1803 or later) or Windows 11, 64-bit, with a GPU that supports Direct3D 11 or later.
- **Linux:** x86-64 with glibc 2.39 or later (for example Ubuntu 24.04 or Fedora 40), and a Vulkan 1.1 GPU driver.
- **macOS:** macOS 12 or later, on an Intel or Apple silicon Mac.
- **Android:** Android 12 or later, 64-bit ARM, Vulkan 1.1.
